tools.name: list_regions
tools.description: Where machines can run. Public, no key needed.

tools.name: list_plans
tools.description: Plans with their resources and prices (hourly and monthly, in CAD). Public, no key needed.

tools.name: list_images
tools.description: Operating systems and ready-to-use application images. The slug is what create_vm expects. Public, no key needed.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Credit balance, hourly burn rate and runway, quota and budget caps. Scope: billing.read.

tools.name: list_vms
tools.description: The account's machines with their status, addresses and billing. Scope: vms.read.

tools.name: get_vm
tools.description: One machine: status, IPv4, IPv6 /64, specs, traffic (Internet only, this traffic month: used_gb, limit_gb, period_ends_at), billing, suspension. Scope: vms.read.

tools.name: get_vm_metrics
tools.description: CPU, memory, disk and network as measured from outside the machine. Scope: vms.read.

tools.name: estimate_vm
tools.description: Runs every check of create_vm and prices it, without creating anything: would_succeed, hourly rate, monthly price, credit required. Call it before create_vm. Scope: vms.create.

tools.name: create_vm
tools.description: Orders a machine and spends credit (hourly) or raises an invoice (monthly). Returns the machine and a provisioning action to poll with get_action. Retrying the same order is safe: it is deduplicated for 24 hours. Scope: vms.create.

tools.name: power_vm
tools.description: start, shutdown (clean ACPI), reboot, or stop (hard power-off). Returns an action to poll with get_action. Scope: vms.action.

tools.name: rename_vm
tools.description: Changes the hostname, inside the guest and in the console. Scope: vms.action.

tools.name: reinstall_vm
tools.description: ERASES THE DISK and redeploys another image. Ask the user first. confirm_hostname must be the machine's exact current hostname. Scope: vms.action.

tools.name: destroy_vm
tools.description: DESTROYS the machine and its disk, with no undo and no backup kept. Ask the user first. confirm_hostname must be the machine's exact hostname. Scope: vms.destroy.

tools.name: get_action
tools.description: Follows an asynchronous action (create, reinstall, power…). Poll until status leaves running; on error it carries the reason. Scope: vms.read.

tools.name: list_vm_actions
tools.description: History of actions on one machine, from the API and the console. Scope: vms.read.

tools.name: get_vm_network
tools.description: IPv4 and IPv6 addresses of a machine with their reverse DNS, and its private networks. Scope: vms.read.

tools.name: set_reverse_dns
tools.description: Sets the PTR record of one of the machine's addresses; null restores the default. Scope: network.write.

tools.name: list_vpcs
tools.description: The account's private networks with their range, gateway and connected machines, plus the quota. Scope: vms.read.

tools.name: get_vpc
tools.description: One private network and the machines on it, with their private address. Scope: vms.read.

tools.name: create_vpc
tools.description: Creates an isolated private network; ready when the call returns. The first usable address (.1) is reserved for the gateway. Scope: network.write.

tools.name: delete_vpc
tools.description: Deletes an empty private network. Refused while a machine is still on it: disconnect or destroy those first. Ask the user first. Scope: network.write.

tools.name: connect_vpc
tools.description: Hot-adds a card on the private network and sets its address in the system, without a restart. configuration: manual means the address must be set by hand in the guest. Connecting again returns the same address. Scope: network.write.

tools.name: disconnect_vpc
tools.description: Removes the machine's private address and card, without a restart. Refused for the only network of a machine with no public address. Scope: network.write.

tools.name: move_vpc
tools.description: Joins the target network, then leaves this one, so the machine is never cut off. Keeps the same address ending when free. Scope: network.write.

tools.name: list_firewalls
tools.description: The account's firewalls with their inbound rules and the machines they protect, plus the quota. Scope: vms.read.

tools.name: get_firewall
tools.description: One firewall: its rules and the machines it protects, with the status of each (applied, pending, error). Scope: vms.read.

tools.name: create_firewall
tools.description: Creates a reusable set of inbound and outbound rules. Without rules it starts with SSH (TCP 22) and ping open from anywhere; pass rules: [] for none. Nothing is filtered until it is attached to a machine. Scope: network.write.

tools.name: update_firewall
tools.description: rules REPLACES the whole list and is applied at once to every attached machine: send every rule to keep, not only the new one (read get_firewall first). Removing the SSH rule can lock the agent out. pending_machines counts machines not updated yet, retried automatically. Scope: network.write.

tools.name: delete_firewall
tools.description: Deletes a firewall attached to no machine. Refused while it protects one: detach it first. Scope: network.write.

tools.name: attach_firewall
tools.description: From now on the machine refuses inbound traffic no rule of its firewalls opens; enforced within about ten seconds of the call. Up to 5 firewalls per machine, rules add up. Refused for a machine with no public address. Attaching again is harmless. Scope: network.write.

tools.name: detach_firewall
tools.description: Removes the firewall's rules from the machine; with no other firewall it accepts all inbound traffic again. Scope: network.write.

tools.name: list_load_balancers
tools.description: The account's load balancers with their addresses, pools, targets and health, listeners and rules, certificates; plus the quota. Scope: vms.read.

tools.name: get_load_balancer
tools.description: One load balancer in full: status, ipv4/ipv6 to put in DNS, pools with targets (health, sessions, response time), listeners with rules in evaluation order, certificates. Scope: vms.read.

tools.name: get_load_balancer_metrics
tools.description: Requests by response class, connections, bytes in/out and peak sessions over 1h (1-minute buckets), 24h (15 minutes) or 7d (1 hour), plus totals. Scope: vms.read.

tools.name: create_load_balancer
tools.description: Orders a load balancer in a private network, billed by the hour from now (the account needs 24 hours of credit), or by the month (7.30 CAD) or the year (73 CAD) with billing. A monthly or yearly period comes out of credit if it covers it; otherwise billing.pending_invoice holds the invoice to pay an

tools.name: delete_load_balancer
tools.description: Deletes the load balancer, its address and its configuration; billing stops. Target machines are not touched. Ask the user first. Scope: vms.destroy.

tools.name: upsert_pool
tools.description: Without pool: creates one (name required, up to 10). With pool: changes only the fields given. Deleting a pool also removes its targets and the rules leading to it. Scope: network.write.

tools.name: delete_pool
tools.description: Removes a pool, its targets and the rules leading to it. Scope: network.write.

tools.name: set_targets
tools.description: REPLACES the pool's targets with exactly this list (up to 25): send every target to keep. Each machine must be in the load balancer's private network (connect_vpc first). drain: true stops new connections to a target before maintenance. Scope: network.write.

tools.name: upsert_listener
tools.description: An entry port on the load balancer's address. Without listener: opens one (port and protocol required, up to 5; 22 and 8402 are reserved). https gets certificates for its rules' hostnames; redirect_https makes port 80 redirect to it. A tcp listener needs a tcp default_pool. sources restricts who may

tools.name: delete_listener
tools.description: Closes the port and removes its rules. Scope: network.write.

tools.name: set_rules
tools.description: REPLACES the http/https listener's rules: each sends a hostname and/or path prefix to an http pool (up to 25). They are evaluated most specific first, whatever the order sent; anything unmatched goes to the default pool. No wildcard hostname on https. Each https hostname gets a certificate once it p

tools.name: list_databases
tools.description: The account's managed databases with their status, private and public addresses, disk, backups and billing (no passwords), plus the quota. Scope: vms.read.

tools.name: get_database_options
tools.description: What can be ordered: engines and versions, extensions, sizes with their hourly, monthly and yearly prices per region, and the price of disk beyond what a size includes. Call it before create_database and show the price to the user. Scope: vms.read.

tools.name: get_database
tools.description: One database: status, connection (host, private ip, port, defaultdb and ffxfadmin; on Valkey no database and default), public access and sources, disk usage and cap, users with their databases (null: all) and read_only, logical databases and extensions, Valkey's eviction policy and data memory, back

tools.name: get_database_credentials
tools.description: Every user with its password, databases and read_only, and its own connection_uri; ready-made connection strings for the admin (private network, and public when open). Treat the result as a secret: give it to the application through an environment variable or a secret store, never into code, commits

tools.name: get_database_metrics
tools.description: CPU, memory, connections and commits per minute (commands per minute on Valkey) over 1h (1-minute buckets), 24h (10 minutes) or 7d (1 hour); only buckets with samples. Scope: vms.read.

tools.name: get_slow_queries
tools.description: The 20 queries with the most total time (pg_stat_statements, values replaced by $1, $2…; performance_schema on MySQL and MariaDB, values replaced by ?): calls, total and mean time, rows. A starting point for indexes. On Valkey, the commands with the most total time since the engine started (GET, HSE

tools.name: list_database_backups
tools.description: Completed backups (weekly full, daily differential; the transaction log is archived continuously) and the restore window: any minute in it can be restored with restore_database. On Valkey, snapshots (rdb) every hour when there were writes, all kept 24 hours, then one a day. Scope: vms.read.

tools.name: create_database
tools.description: Orders a managed database (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB or Valkey) in a private network, billed by the hour from now (the account needs 24 hours of credit), or by the month (730 hours) or the year (ten months) with billing; get_database_options gives each price. A monthly or yearly period comes out of

tools.name: restore_database
tools.description: Creates a NEW database, billed like any other, holding the data as it was at a given minute of the source's restore window (list_database_backups; Valkey: the last snapshot before that minute), with the same users and passwords. The source is not touched and may have been deleted in the last 7 days.

tools.name: fork_database
tools.description: Creates a NEW database, billed like any other, whose data is an instant copy of this one (for a test or staging copy), with the same users and passwords. It stays linked to its source for up to 7 days (no backups of its own, the source cannot be deleted) unless detach_database_fork ends that sooner.

tools.name: detach_database_fork
tools.description: Gives a linked fork its own copy of the data; the database is unavailable for about 30 seconds, then its backups start. Scope: vms.action.

tools.name: resize_database
tools.description: Moves the database to a LARGER size (more vCPU, memory and included disk; see get_database_options): same data, users, names and addresses. It restarts: one to two minutes of downtime, status maintenance meanwhile (resize.to_gb set), then active with the new size_gb. The new rate applies from the ne

tools.name: delete_database
tools.description: DELETES the database and its data; billing stops. Ask the user first. confirm_name must be the database's exact name. Its backups stay 7 days (restore_database can bring it back meanwhile). Refused while a linked fork depends on it. Scope: vms.destroy.

tools.name: update_database
tools.description: Any of: the name; the weekly maintenance window (day 0 = Sunday, start hour, Montréal time, 2 hours long; minor updates, usually under 2 minutes of downtime); the disk cap (the disk grows by itself at 80 % full, up to the cap; disk beyond what the size includes is billed per GB); on Valkey, the evic

tools.name: set_database_public_access
tools.description: Opens the database to the internet at its public host and port (IPv4 and IPv6, TLS and password still required), or closes it. sources restricts who may connect (IPv4/IPv6 addresses or ranges); omitted it is left as is, null or [] means everyone. Prefer listing the user's addresses. Live within abou

tools.name: backup_database
tools.description: Starts a differential backup within a minute, e.g. before a risky migration. Not available on a linked fork. Scope: backups.write.

tools.name: create_database_user
tools.description: Creates a user with a generated password, returned here once (also readable with get_database_credentials); live within seconds. Up to 30 users. It connects only to its databases (every logical database, future ones included, when databases is omitted): it reads and writes everything there and creat

tools.name: set_database_user_access
tools.description: Sets the logical databases a user connects to (databases: a list, or null for all of them, future ones included) and whether it only reads; a field left out keeps its value. Applied within seconds; where its access is removed or lowered, its open connections are closed, so tell the user first if an

tools.name: reset_database_password
tools.description: Gives the user a new password, returned here; the old one stops working within seconds, so update the application first or right after. Scope: databases.write.

tools.name: delete_database_user
tools.description: Hands the user's objects to the admin, then drops the user. The admin (ffxfadmin, or default on Valkey) cannot be deleted. Scope: databases.write.

tools.name: create_logical_database
tools.description: Creates another database inside the managed database (like defaultdb), owned by the admin; up to 30. Not on Valkey (numbered databases, SELECT 0 to 15). Scope: databases.write.

tools.name: delete_logical_database
tools.description: DROPS the logical database with everything in it (the backups keep it 7 days). Ask the user first. Scope: databases.write.

tools.name: enable_extension
tools.description: PostgreSQL only. Enables an extension from get_database_options (vector for pgvector, postgis, pg_trgm…) in one logical database; installed on demand, live within a minute. Scope: databases.write.

tools.name: disable_extension
tools.description: Drops the extension without CASCADE: if objects depend on it, it stays and get_database shows why in warning. Scope: databases.write.

tools.name: get_runners
tools.description: The runs-on labels with their vCPU, memory and price per minute, the account's concurrency (vCPU of jobs starting or running, and the cap), the linked GitHub organizations and accounts, this month's minutes and cost per repository, the actions cache next to the runners (bytes, entries and last use p

tools.name: list_runner_jobs
tools.description: Jobs that ran or wait on FFxF runners, most recent first: repository, workflow and job, label, status (queued with waiting_reason credit, budget or account; running; succeeded; failed, stopped_for_credit when the credit ran out; cancelled; refused with refusal), times, billed minutes and amount, lin

tools.name: list_ssh_keys
tools.description: SSH keys saved on the account, to pass to create_vm. Scope: sshkeys.write or vms.read.

tools.name: add_ssh_key
tools.description: Saves a public key on the account so new machines can be reached without a password. Scope: sshkeys.write.

tools.name: delete_ssh_key
tools.description: Removes a key from the account. Machines already deployed with it keep it; only future deployments change. Scope: sshkeys.write.
